steps.explanationAfterStep: The complex is the electrophile of bromination: the arene attacks the outer bromine and AlBr₄⁻ leaves. AlBr₃ is regenerated at the end, so it is a catalyst.

title: Activating bromine with AlBr₃
subtitle: A Lewis acid turns Br₂ into a source of Br⁺
references: Clayden, Greeves and Warren, Organic Chemistry, 2nd edition (Oxford University Press), chapter 21

reactants.caption: bromine + aluminium bromide
hintTiers: Aluminium in AlBr₃ has only six valence electrons. What can fill its empty orbital?
A lone pair on one bromine of Br₂ forms a bond to aluminium. One arrow.
A lone pair on one bromine → a new Br–Al bond.
reactants.learnerPrompt: Benzene is too weak a nucleophile for Br₂ alone. Show how AlBr₃ activates it.

misconceptions.feedbackMessage: AlBr₃ is the electron-poor partner: it accepts a pair, it does not give one. Start from a bromine lone pair.
Br₂ does not split into Br⁺ and Br⁻ on its own. The Lewis acid first takes a lone pair.

mechanismSummary: A lone pair on bromine fills the empty orbital of aluminium. The Br–Br bond is now strongly polarised: the outer bromine behaves as Br⁺ towards an arene. FeBr₃ does the same job; AlBr₃ is drawn here.
